name: 郑和
oneLiner: 七下西洋，以当时世界最大的宝船舰队远抵东非，比欧洲大航海早近一个世纪。
oneLinerEn: Seven voyages to the Western Oceans with the era's largest treasure fleets, reaching East Africa nearly a century before European expansion.
bio: 宦官出身的回族航海家，受明成祖之命通使西洋，载和平交往而非殖民征服，留下精密的远洋航海图。
bioEn: A Muslim eunuch admiral who, on Ming Emperor Yongle's orders, sailed for diplomacy not conquest, leaving detailed charts of the ocean routes.

ideas.v: 船体规模与航海组织远超同期。
ideas.vEn: Fleet scale and organization surpassed contemporaries.

ideas.v: 以朝贡与贸易立信，未殖民据点。
ideas.vEn: Built trust via tribute and trade, no colonial footholds.

quotes.q: 欲报效国家，惟以航海通达四方。
quotes.qEn: To serve the state, I would sail the seas and reach all quarters.

name: 郦道元
oneLiner: 为《水经》作注，足迹遍及南北，写成兼具地理、水文与人文的《水经注》。
oneLinerEn: Annotated the Waterways Classic, traversing north and south to produce the geographically and culturally rich Commentary on the Waterways Classic.
bio: 以实地考察补正旧说，记录河流源流、地貌与风俗，开中国系统描述地理之先河。
bioEn: He corrected old texts through field study, recording river courses, landforms and customs, pioneering systematic descriptive geography in China.

ideas.v: 以河流为线索串连区域地理。
ideas.vEn: Used rivers to organize regional geography.

ideas.v: 重亲历、轻因袭。
ideas.vEn: Valued firsthand observation over inherited claims.

quotes.q: 山水有灵，亦当惊知己于千古。
quotes.qEn: If mountains and rivers have spirit, they would be glad of a kindred mind across the ages.

name: 徐霞客
oneLiner: 三十年遍游名山大川，尤以对喀斯特地貌的系统记录早于西方两个世纪。
oneLinerEn: Thirty years traversing China's mountains and rivers, his systematic karst records predating the West by two centuries.
bio: 弃科举而游历，以日记详记地形、洞穴与植被，留下《徐霞客游记》这一地理与旅行奇书。
bioEn: He abandoned the exam path for travel, logging terrain, caves and vegetation in Xu Xiake's Travels, a geographic and literary marvel.

ideas.v: 详述峰林、溶洞与地下河。
ideas.vEn: Detailed peaks, caves and underground rivers.

ideas.v: 以日记数十年实地观察。
ideas.vEn: Decades of dated, on-site observation.

quotes.q: 达人所之未达，探人所之未知。
quotes.qEn: Reach where others have not, probe what others do not know.

name: 竺可桢
oneLiner: 中国现代地理学与气象学奠基人，以长期物候与气候序列研究著称。
oneLinerEn: Founder of modern geography and meteorology in China, known for long-term phenology and climate-series research.
bio: 创建气象与地理研究机构，倡导以连续观测积累中国气候本底，奠定实证研究基础。
bioEn: He founded meteorological and geographic institutions, championing continuous observation to establish China's climatic baseline.

ideas.v: 以长序列揭示季风与变迁。
ideas.vEn: Long records revealing monsoons and change.

ideas.v: 以物候指示季节与农时。
ideas.vEn: Used phenology to mark seasons and farming.

works.title: 中国近五千年来气候变迁的初步研究
works.titleEn: Preliminary Study on Climate Change in China over the Last 5000 Years

quotes.q: 科学之使命，在求真与致用。
quotes.qEn: The mission of science is truth and usefulness.

name: 亚历山大·冯·洪堡
oneLiner: 现代地理学奠基人之一，提出「自然总体」观念，把气候、植被与海拔连成统一图景。
oneLinerEn: A founder of modern geography who framed nature as a unified whole, linking climate, vegetation and altitude.
bio: 南美科考五载，登钦博拉索、绘等温线，开创用测量与比较理解地球的方法，深刻影响达尔文与生态思想。
bioEn: Five years surveying South America, climbing Chimborazo and drawing isotherms; his measured, comparative method deeply influenced Darwin and ecology.

ideas.v: 万物相互关联，须整体考察。
ideas.vEn: All things are connected; study as a whole.

ideas.v: 以温度分布重构气候认知。
ideas.vEn: Reframed climate via temperature distribution.

quotes.q: 自然是活的整体，而非死物拼凑。
quotes.qEn: Nature is a living whole, not a dead assemblage.

name: 麦哲伦
oneLiner: 率领船队完成首次环球航行（本人途中殁于菲律宾），实证了地球之大与海洋之连。
oneLinerEn: Led the first circumnavigation (dying en route in the Philippines), proving the Earth's size and the oceans' connection.
bio: 为西班牙西航寻香料之路，穿麦哲伦海峡入太平洋；其船队返航确认了全球航行的可能。
bioEn: Sailing west for Spain, he crossed the strait into the Pacific; his fleet's return confirmed global circumnavigation.

ideas.v: 用航行证明地球是球体且海洋相连。
ideas.vEn: Proved by sail that Earth is round and oceans connect.

ideas.v: 横渡时称其「平静之海」。
ideas.vEn: Named the ocean 'Pacific' for its calm crossing.

quotes.q: 大海，是连接世界最辽阔的道路。
quotes.qEn: The sea is the broadest road that connects the world.

name: 戴维·利文斯通
oneLiner: 深入非洲内陆、勘明赞比西河与维多利亚瀑布，也以反对奴隶贸易闻名。
oneLinerEn: Penetrated the African interior, mapping the Zambezi and Victoria Falls, and campaigned against the slave trade.
bio: 传教士兼探险家，三入非洲，绘制大量未知地图；其失踪与斯坦利「我找到你了」成为传奇。
bioEn: Missionary-explorer who mapped vast unknown regions; his disappearance and Stanley's 'Dr. Livingstone, I presume?' became legend.

ideas.v: 首次系统绘出中部非洲水系。
ideas.vEn: First systematic mapping of central African waters.

ideas.v: 以探险揭示奴隶贸易之害。
ideas.vEn: Used exploration to expose the slave trade's evils.

quotes.q: 我愿为非洲的开放与文明倾尽一生。
quotes.qEn: I will lay down my life for the opening of Africa to civilization.

name: 雅克-伊夫·库斯托
oneLiner: 发明水肺、拍出《寂静的世界》，把深海带给大众并唤起海洋保护意识。
oneLinerEn: Co-invented the aqua-lung and filmed The Silent World, bringing the deep to the public and awakening ocean conservation.
bio: 海军军官转型的海洋先驱，驾「卡里普索」号环游世界，用影像让亿万观众第一次看见海底。
bioEn: A naval officer turned ocean pioneer, he sailed the Calypso and showed billions the seabed for the first time.

ideas.v: 让人类自由潜入水下呼吸。
ideas.vEn: Let humans breathe freely underwater.

ideas.v: 以影像推动海洋保护立法。
ideas.vEn: Used film to push ocean-protection law.

quotes.q: 人类若不懂得海洋，便不懂这颗星球。
quotes.qEn: People protect what they love; to love the sea, they must know it.

name: 伊本·白图泰
oneLiner: 三十年游历亚非欧四十余国，行程数万公里，留下中世纪最详尽的旅行见闻录。
oneLinerEn: Across three decades he visited over forty countries in Africa, Asia and Europe, leaving the era's richest travel account.
bio: 出身法学之家，本为朝觐出发，却走到中国、东非与金帐汗国；其游记是研究中世纪世界的珍贵史料。
bioEn: A jurist who set out to pilgrimage and reached China, East Africa and the Golden Horde; his Rihla is priceless medieval history.

ideas.v: 亲历从北非到中国的商旅网络。
ideas.vEn: Witnessed the trade networks from North Africa to China.

ideas.v: 以亲见记录城市、风俗与航路。
ideas.vEn: Recorded cities, customs and seaways from personal sight.

quotes.q: 旅行，是摘下面具、看见世界最好的方式。
quotes.qEn: Travel is the best way to remove masks and see the world.

name: 托勒密
oneLiner: 在《地理学指南》中以经纬网绘制已知世界，地图范式影响欧洲千年。
oneLinerEn: In the Geography he mapped the known world on a graticule, a cartographic paradigm that shaped Europe for a millennium.
bio: 集希腊—罗马地理知识大成，以数学化方式整理地名与坐标，其地图虽有误却主导中世纪认知。
bioEn: Synthesizing Greco-Roman geography, he organized places mathematically; his maps, though flawed, dominated medieval thought.

ideas.v: 用经纬度定位，奠定制图科学。
ideas.vEn: Located places by lat/long, founding map science.

ideas.v: 系统汇编可居住世界的地理。
ideas.vEn: Systematically compiled the inhabited world's geography.

quotes.q: 要以数学的精确，描绘大地应有的样子。
quotes.qEn: Depict the Earth as it is, with mathematical precision.

name: 埃拉托色尼
country: 古希腊（昔兰尼—亚历山大）
oneLiner: 用两城日影差与距离，首次较准确测算出地球周长，并创「地理学」一词。
oneLinerEn: Using shadow angles at two cities, he first measured Earth's circumference with surprising accuracy and coined 'geography'.
bio: 亚历山大图书馆馆长，学问横跨数学、天文与地理，以简洁实验逼近地球尺度。
bioEn: Chief librarian at Alexandria, he spanned math, astronomy and geography, approximating Earth's size with a simple experiment.

ideas.v: 日影差法估得地球周长近真值。
ideas.vEn: Shadow-difference method neared the true circumference.

ideas.v: 首创以「地理」统摄大地之学。
ideas.vEn: First named the study of the Earth 'geography'.

quotes.q: 想知道大地多大，先学会仰望太阳。
quotes.qEn: To know Earth's size, first look up at the sun.

name: 段义孚
oneLiner: 把地理学带回「人的感受」：抽象空间被赋予意义才成为「地方」，人对土地的爱与惧值得一再研究。
oneLinerEn: He brought feeling back into geography: abstract space becomes 'place' only when laden with meaning, and people's love of and dread toward the land deserve study.
bio: 明尼苏达大学教授，人文主义地理学的奠基人之一。他反对把地理简化为数字与模型，主张研究人如何体验、并赋予地方以意义：冰冷的「空间」经由情感与记忆的投注，化为有归属感的「地方」；「恋地情结（topophilia）」是人对环境的依恋之爱，「恐惧之地」则相反。他关注身体、家园、尺度与时间如何层层编织出「地方感」，让地理学重新与文学、现象学和心理学对话，也深刻影响了关于归属感、家园与环境感知的研究。
bioEn: A professor at the University of Minnesota and a founder of humanistic geography. Against reducing geography to numbers and models, he studied how people experience and endow places with meaning: cold 'space' turns into a belonging-laden 'place' through the investment of feeling and memory, while 'topophilia' names our love of the environment and feared places its inverse. Attending to how body, home, scale and time weave a sense of place, he reopened geography's dialogue with literature, phenomenology and psychology and deeply shaped the study of belonging, home and environmental perception.

ideas.v: 人对自然环境的多重依恋之爱，从感官愉悦到精神归属。
ideas.vEn: People's layered love of the natural environment, from sensory delight to spiritual belonging.

ideas.v: 空间经体验与赋义而成人所依附的「地方」。
ideas.vEn: Space, lived and endowed with meaning, becomes the 'place' people cling to.

ideas.v: 从身体、居所到社区与宇宙，层层展开的意义圈。
ideas.vEn: From body and dwelling to community and cosmos, concentric circles of meaning.

works.title: 空间与地方：经验的视角
works.titleEn: Space and Place: The Perspective of Experience

quotes.q: 地方是被注入了意义的空间。
quotes.qEn: A place is space that has been filled with meaning.

name: 阿尔弗雷德·魏格纳
oneLiner: 以气象学家之身撼动地质学：大陆如浮筏漂移，曾拼合为一块「泛大陆」——生前见斥，身后成范式。
oneLinerEn: A meteorologist who shook geology: continents drift like rafts and once joined as one 'Pangaea'—rejected in his life, vindicated as a paradigm after.
bio: 德国气象与地球物理学家。1912 年他据大西洋两岸海岸线的吻合、相同古生物与植物化石的跨洋分布、以及古冰川遗迹的对应，提出「大陆漂移说」：远古大陆曾连为「泛大陆（Pangaea）」，其后裂解、漂移至今位。因当时无法说明漂移的动力来源，此说长期被地质学界斥为异想天开；直到 1960 年代海底扩张与板块构造论确立，他的直觉才被证实，奉为先驱。1930 年他殉职于格陵兰冰原考察。
bioEn: A German meteorologist and geophysicist. In 1912, from the fit of the coastlines on either side of the Atlantic, the trans-oceanic match of identical fossils and the correspondence of ancient glacial traces, he proposed continental drift: the landmasses once formed a single 'Pangaea' that later split and moved apart. Unable to name the force that drove them, the idea was long dismissed by geologists as fantasy; only in the 1960s, with seafloor spreading and plate tectonics, was his intuition confirmed and honored as prophetic. He died on a Greenland ice-field expedition in 1930.

ideas.v: 大陆并非固定，而是在地幔上缓慢横向移动。
ideas.vEn: Continents are not fixed but creep sideways over the mantle.

ideas.v: 所有大陆曾拼合为一整块，后逐级裂解分离。
ideas.vEn: All land once joined a single mass that later broke stepwise apart.

ideas.v: 海岸拟合、相同化石与冰川遗迹共同指向曾经相连。
ideas.vEn: Fitting coasts, matching fossils and glacial relics all point to past union.

works.title: 海陆的起源
works.titleEn: The Origin of Continents and Oceans

quotes.q: 大陆并非固定，而是漂移开去。
quotes.qEn: The continents are not fixed but have drifted apart.

name: 哈尔福德·麦金德
oneLiner: 「谁主宰心脏地带，谁就统治世界岛」——把地理权力写进大国战略的经典地缘政治学家。
oneLinerEn: 'Who rules the Heartland commands the World-Island'—the classic geopolitician who wrote geographic power into grand strategy.
bio: 英国地理学家与政治学者，地缘政治学的奠基人之一。1904 年论文《历史的地理枢纽》提出「心脏地带（Heartland）」：欧亚大陆腹心那片海洋权力难以企及的平原，随铁路的机动能力而崛起为陆权的源头，并留下著名推论——统治东欧者主宰心脏地带，主宰心脏地带者主宰「世界岛」（欧亚非），主宰世界岛者主宰世界。他的陆权思想深刻塑造了二十世纪对德、俄战略的想象，也因「地理决定」的色彩而广受批评。
bioEn: A British geographer and political scholar, a founder of geopolitics. His 1904 paper The Geographical Pivot of History posited the 'Heartland'—the sea-power-inaccessible plains of Eurasia's core, rising as the fount of land power with the mobility of rail—and left the famous chain: who rules Eastern Europe commands the Heartland, who rules the Heartland commands the 'World-Island' (Eurasia-Africa), who rules the World-Island commands the world. His land-power vision deeply shaped twentieth-century strategic thinking about Germany and Russia, and was much criticized for its geographic determinism.

ideas.v: 欧亚腹心的陆权堡垒，海权难以直接控制。
ideas.vEn: The land-power citadel of Eurasia's interior, hard for sea power to reach.

ideas.v: 机动技术决定大陆腹地与海洋边缘的此消彼长。
ideas.vEn: Mobility tech sets the rise and fall of the continental core and maritime rim.

ideas.v: 欧亚非连成一体的巨大陆块，是人类文明的重心。
ideas.vEn: The joined mass of Eurasia-Africa, the weight-center of world history.

quotes.q: 谁统治东欧，谁就主宰心脏地带。
quotes.qEn: Who rules East Europe commands the Heartland.

name: 卡尔·李特尔
oneLiner: 与洪堡并肩使地理学成为独立学科：以「区域」为单位，追问地球如何成为人类的家园。
oneLinerEn: Beside Humboldt he made geography a discipline in its own right—working region by region to ask how the earth became humankind's home.
bio: 德国地理学家、柏林大学首任地理学教授，常与洪堡并列为现代地理学奠基人。若说洪堡偏重「通用／自然」地理，李特尔则专注「地志／区域」与人和地的关系，主张把地球当作人类历史的舞台来比较研究，强调一方之内自然与人文现象的相互关联。其多卷巨著《地理学——地球与人类历史的关系》系统比较各大洲，被视为「人地关系」思想的重要源头；其论述亦带有目的论与神学色彩，为后世所批评。
bioEn: A German geographer and the first professor of geography at Berlin, ranked with Humboldt as a founder of modern geography. Where Humboldt leaned toward general/physical geography, Ritter focused on regional chorography and the human–land bond, treating the earth as the stage of human history to be studied comparatively and stressing the interconnection of natural and human phenomena within each region. His voluminous Geography set out to compare the world's continents and is seen as a key source of human-land thinking, though its teleological and theological coloring drew later criticism.

ideas.v: 以区域为单位，比较各地球体独特的自然—人文关联。
ideas.vEn: Taking regions as units, comparing each land's unique nature–culture web.

ideas.v: 自然塑造人居与历史，地理是「家园」的科学。
ideas.vEn: Nature molds settlement and history; geography is the science of home.

ideas.v: 在各大洲的对照中归纳地球与人互动的规律。
ideas.vEn: Gathering the laws of earth–human interaction across the continents.

works.title: 地理学——地球与人类历史的关系

quotes.q: 地球是人类历史的舞台。
quotes.qEn: The earth is the stage of human history.

name: 詹姆斯·赫顿
oneLiner: 「深时间」之父：以今日之缓变读出地球之悠远，均变论悄然把地质学从神创年表中解放。
oneLinerEn: Father of "deep time": reading Earth's vast age in today's slow change, uniformitarianism quietly freed geology from scriptural chronologies.
bio: 苏格兰自然哲学家，在爱丁堡与锡卡湾的实地观察中领悟：一些「找不到起点、也望不见终点」的过程，正一点点雕琢着地表。他「以今日解过去」的思路为莱尔所总结，也为达尔文所需的漫长时间打开了大门。
bioEn: A Scottish natural philosopher, he saw at Edinburgh and Siccar Bay that processes with "no vestige of a beginning, no prospect of an end" were slowly shaping the surface. His "key to the past lies in the present" was summed up by Lyell and opened the vast time Darwin would need.

ideas.v: 地球的年纪远超圣经推算的数千年。
ideas.vEn: Earth is far older than the few thousand years of scriptural counts.

ideas.v: 今日缓慢的自然作用是解读过去的钥匙。
ideas.vEn: Today's slow natural action is the key to reading the past.

ideas.v: 岩石由地下热反复熔融、抬升而成。
ideas.vEn: Rocks are remelted and uplifted by subterranean heat.

quotes.q: 我们找不到起点，也望不见终点。
quotes.qEn: We find no vestige of a beginning, no prospect of an end.

name: 查尔斯·莱尔
oneLiner: 以《地质学原理》把均变论铸成地学方法：现在是理解过去的钥匙，为达尔文的缓慢演化备好时间舞台。
oneLinerEn: With his Principles of Geology he forged uniformitarianism into method—the present as key to the past—laying the slow stage Darwin would need.
bio: 苏格兰律师转业的地质学家。三卷《地质学原理》以实证集束证明：地表由地震、火山、侵蚀这些今日仍在运作之力，历经难以想象之久逐渐塑成，深深影响了在环球航船上研读其书的达尔文。
bioEn: A Scottish lawyer-turned-geologist. His three-volume Principles of Geology showed by evidence that the surface is shaped, over immense time, by earthquakes, volcanoes and erosion still at work today—profoundly swaying Darwin, who read it aboard the Beagle.

ideas.v: 用今日可见的作用去解释过去。
ideas.vEn: Explain the past by causes visible today.

ideas.v: 微小的力量久叠足以移山填海。
ideas.vEn: Minute forces, piled over ages, move mountains.

ideas.v: 地球既没有创世之日，也没有既定终局。
ideas.vEn: Earth has no creation day nor fixed final state.

quotes.q: 看清当下，方能读懂往昔。
quotes.qEn: The present is the key to the past.

name: 马修·莫里
oneLiner: 「海洋学之父」：汇集千船航海日志，绘出首幅风与洋流图，把空旷大洋变成有路可循的蓝径。
oneLinerEn: The "father of oceanography": compiling a thousand ships' logs into the first wind and current charts, he turned open ocean into blue roads with routes to follow.
bio: 美国海军军官，因伤转掌航海仪器库，系统收集商船观测，出版《海洋的物理地理学》与洋流、风场图，大幅缩短航程；并借为跨洋电缆所做的海底测量，提供了深海平坦的最初线索。
bioEn: A US naval officer who, after injury, ran the depot of charts and instruments and gathered merchantmen's observations into his Physical Geography of the Seas with current and wind charts—shortening voyages and, from soundings taken for cables, hinting at a flat deep seafloor.

ideas.v: 风与流并非杂乱，可测、可图、可循。
ideas.vEn: Winds and currents are law-governed—measurable, chartable, sailable.

ideas.v: 千船日志汇成一幅全球图景。
ideas.vEn: A thousand logs combine into one global picture.

works.title: 海洋的物理地理学
works.titleEn: The Physical Geography of the Seas

quotes.q: 绘制了风与流的道路，便缩短了海洋的航程。
quotes.qEn: Chart the roads of wind and current, and the sea's voyages grow shorter.

name: 哈里·赫斯
oneLiner: 海底扩张的提出者：洋壳在海岭涌出、向两侧铺展、潜没而亡——为大陆漂移补上它欠下的动力。
oneLinerEn: Proposer of seafloor spreading: new crust wells up at ridges, spreads sideways, and sinks to its death—giving continental drift the engine it had lacked.
bio: 美国地质学家与海军少将，普林斯顿教授任内兼率潜艇考察，据声呐测深发现大洋中脊与中央裂谷、以及深海平原之年轻；1962 年以《大洋盆地史》提出海底扩张，与同期古地磁条带证据一道催生了板块构造论。
bioEn: An American geologist and rear admiral who, as Princeton professor, captained submarine surveys; from sonar soundings he found mid-ocean ridges with central rifts and young abyssal plains, and in 1962 his History of Ocean Basins proposed seafloor spreading which, with magnetic stripes, midwifed plate tectonics.

ideas.v: 新洋壳在海岭生成，对称向两侧推开。
ideas.vEn: New crust forms at ridges and splits symmetrically outward.

ideas.v: 海底远较大陆为新，最老不过约两亿年。
ideas.vEn: The seafloor is far younger than continents—nothing older than some 200 Myr.

ideas.v: 在海沟处旧壳下沉，重回地幔。
ideas.vEn: At trenches old crust sinks back into the mantle.

quotes.q: 大陆并非在漂移，而是被新生的海底推着走。
quotes.qEn: Continents don't drift—they are carried along by spreading new seafloor.
